composers.name: Tyagaraja
composers.style: Bhakti-oriented, expressive, simple yet profound melodies (sangatis).
composers.famous_works: Pancharatna Kritis, Utsava Sampradaya Kritis, Prahlada Bhakti Vijayam
composers.influence: Popularised the Kriti format with sangatis (melodic variations). Deeply influenced modern concert structure.

composers.name: Muthuswami Dikshitar
composers.style: Scholarly, slow tempo (chauka kala), intricate gamakas, structural grandeur, inclusion of raga mudras.
composers.famous_works: Navagraha Kritis, Kamalamba Navavarana Kritis, Nottuswaras
composers.influence: Brought Hindustani ragas to Carnatic music. Master of scholarly, slow-paced compositions.

composers.name: Syama Sastri
composers.style: Rhythmic complexity (tala mastery), deeply emotional, use of rare ragas and viloma chapu tala.
composers.influence: Known for his unmatched mastery over complex talas like Misra Chapu. Architect of the modern Swarajati.

composers.name: Purandaradasa
composers.style: Foundational Carnatic teaching exercises (Sarali, Jantai), devotional padas, accessible philosophy.
composers.influence: Known as the Pitamaha (Grandfather) of Carnatic music. Structured the basic lessons (Sarali, Jantai) in Mayamalavagowla.

composers.name: Swathi Thirunal
composers.style: Royal patronage, mastery of diverse musical forms (Kriti, Padam, Varnam, Tillana, Dhrupad).
composers.famous_works: Navaratri Kritis, Navavidha Bhakti Kritis, Utsava Prabandhas
composers.influence: Royal patron who composed in diverse languages and forms, including Hindustani Dhrupad and Khayal.

composers.name: Annamacharya
composers.style: Pioneer of the Sankirtana format (Pallavi + Charanas), profound devotion, social themes.
composers.famous_works: Sringara Sankirtanas, Adhyatma Sankirtanas (e.g., Brahmam Okate)
composers.influence: First known composer of the Sankirtana format. Immense cultural impact on Telugu literature and devotion.

composers.name: Saint Tyagaraja
composers.biography: One of the greatest composers of Carnatic music, part of the Trinity. Wrote thousands of Telugu kritis in praise of Lord Rama.

composers.name: Swati Tirunal
composers.biography: Maharaja of Travancore who composed in multiple languages (Sanskrit, Telugu, Hindi, Malayalam) including beautiful padams and varnams.

composers.name: Bhadrachala Ramadasu
composers.biography: Telugu composer of Ramadasu Kirtanas who laid the path for Tyagaraja's Rama-bhakti.

composers.name: Papanasam Sivan
composers.biography: Prolific composer of Tamil kritis and film songs, often called 'Tamil Tyagaraja'.

composers.name: Patnam Subramania Iyer
composers.biography: Great composer of varnams and kritis, who trained many legendary disciples.

composers.name: Gopalakrishna Bharathi
composers.biography: Famous for his Tamil opera 'Nandanar Charitram' and songs in praise of Lord Shiva.

composers.name: Muthiah Bhagavatar
composers.biography: Prolific composer who popularized many rare ragas and composed the Chamundamba Ashtottara kritis.

composers.name: Mysore Vasudevachar
composers.biography: Eminent composer in Telugu and Sanskrit, disciple of Patnam Subramania Iyer, known for graceful melodies.

composers.name: Koteeswara Iyer
composers.biography: First to compose kritis in all 72 Melakarta ragas in the Tamil language.

composers.name: Subbaraya Sastri
composers.biography: Son of Syama Sastri, who studied under all three Trinity members and composed highly refined kritis.

composers.name: Maha Vaidyanatha Iyer
composers.biography: Legendary vocalist who composed the grand 72 Melaragamalika in a single performance.

composers.name: Ramanathapuram Srinivasa Iyengar
composers.biography: Also known as Poochi Srinivasa Iyengar, composed legendary varnams and jawalis.

composers.name: Oothukkadu Venkata Kavi
composers.biography: Brilliant composer who wrote beautiful compositions (Kamakhya Navavarana, Saptaratna) with intricate rhythmic patterns.

composers.name: G N Balasubramaniam
composers.biography: Vocalist and composer who introduced rapid tempos and modern structural aesthetics into compositions.

composers.name: Lalgudi Jayaraman
composers.biography: Violin virtuoso who composed incredibly popular varnams, thillanas, and pushpanjalis.

composers.name: Balamuralikrishna
composers.biography: Legendary musician who composed in all 72 melakartas, created new ragas, and wrote beautiful varnams and thillanas.

talas.name: Adi Tala
talas.description: The most common tala in Carnatic music, representing a Chatusra Jaati Triputa Tala.

talas.name: Rupaka Tala
talas.description: A very popular fast-paced tala, widely used for lively kritis and varnams.

talas.name: Misra Chapu Tala
talas.description: An asymmetric, highly syncopated and rhythmic tala of folk origin, highly favored by Syama Sastri.

talas.name: Khanda Chapu Tala
talas.description: A beautiful 5-beat rhythm popular in both classical and semi-classical devotional songs.

talas.name: Ata Tala
talas.angas: 2 Laghus (5 beats each in Khanda Jati) + 2 Drutams
talas.description: A grand, long rhythmic cycle, most famous for its use in heavy, majestic Varnams (e.g. Viriboni in Bhairavi).

talas.name: Jhampa Tala
talas.angas: 1 Laghu (7 beats) + 1 Anudrutam (1 beat) + 1 Drutam (2 beats)
talas.description: A standard 10-beat cycle in the Suladi Sapta Tala system.

talas.name: Triputa Tala
talas.description: A heptatonic cycle; when the Laghu is Chatusra (4 beats) it becomes Adi Tala.

shruti.1.5: C# / D-flat (Between 1 & 2 Kattai / ~269.3 Hz — used by some vocalists for a mid-low pitch)
shruti.2: C# / D-flat (Safed Do / Tonic at ~277.2 Hz)
shruti.2.5: D / D# (Between 2 & 3 Kattai / ~285.3 Hz — a commonly chosen comfortable mid-pitch)
shruti.3.5: D# / E-flat (Between 3 & 4 Kattai / ~302.3 Hz — preferred by many female vocalists)
shruti.4: D# / E-flat (Safed Char / Tonic at ~311.1 Hz)
shruti.4.5: E / F (Between 4 & 5 Kattai / ~320.2 Hz — frequently used concert pitch for male vocalists)
shruti.5.5: F / F# (Between 5 & 6 Kattai / ~339.4 Hz — higher pitch for bright, resonant concert effect)
shruti.6.5: F# / G-flat (Between 6 & 7 Kattai / ~359.7 Hz — used for high-pitched traditional renditions)
shruti.7: F# / G-flat (Safed Sat / Tonic at ~370.0 Hz)

pancharatna.description: The first Pancharatna kriti. Composed entirely in majestic Sanskrit. It praises Lord Rama with 108 names and acts as a grand musical invocation.
The second Pancharatna kriti. Written in expressive Telugu. The composer lists various human flaws, self-indulgences, and errors, asking Lord Rama for ultimate redemption.
The third Pancharatna kriti. Composed in a cheerful and bright Arabhi scale. It describes the playful deeds and divine tricks of Lord Krishna, celebrating how the Lord always triumphs.

The fourth Pancharatna kriti. Composed in the deeply emotional and heavy Varali raga. It describes the exquisite beauty of Lord Rama, singing that the more one beholds the Lord, the more beautiful He appears.
The crowning fifth Pancharatna kriti in the auspicious Sri raga. It is a universal salute to all great souls, seers, and musicians of all times, expressing deep devotion and humility.

cross_tradition_mappings.evidence: Hindustani Bhairavi corresponds to Carnatic Thodi in terms of aroha and avaroha
Both are major pentatonic scales using the same five notes
Both use Lydian mode with same scale. Kalyani is S R2 G3 M2 P D2 N3 and Yaman uses all shuddh swaras except tivra Ma
Standard equivalents with same pentatonic set
